papers.title: DRAMP 2.0, an updated data repository of antimicrobial peptides
Deep-AmPEP30: Improve Short Antimicrobial Peptides Prediction with Deep Learning
Prediction of antimicrobial peptides toxicity based on their physico-chemical properties using machine learning techniques
CalcAMP: A New Machine Learning Model for the Accurate Prediction of Antimicrobial Activity of Peptides

models.architecture_or_algorithm: Machine learning model based on 3D descriptors (specific algorithm not named)
models.candidate_reason: Described as a predictive classifier for AMPs, with reported performance, but lacks name and public code; may be available in future DRAMP updates.
blocking_issues: No code or web server link available
Not yet integrated into DRAMP as stated

models.architecture_or_algorithm: Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) with PseKRAAC reduced amino acid composition features
models.input_features: PseKRAAC reduced amino acid composition (86 features from five-best clusters)
models.dataset_source_or_link: Benchmark dataset of 188 samples (balanced); training set of 1529 positive samples from AMP databases (AmPEP, etc.)
models.candidate_reason: Publicly available web server for short AMP prediction, including genome screening; strong experimental validation; suitable for benchmarking.

models.architecture_or_algorithm: Hybrid model combining SVC (RBF), Random Forest, etc., with feature selection
models.input_features: Combination of physico-chemical and linguistic-based features (90 selected features including aggregation propensity, polar residue composition, etc.)
models.candidate_reason: This model predicts AMP toxicity, not AMP identity. It is relevant for downstream filtering but not for direct AMP prediction benchmark.
blocking_issues: Focus on toxicity rather than antimicrobial activity classification

models.architecture_or_algorithm: Ensemble tree-based algorithms (CatBoost, LightGBM, XGBoost, Random Forest) with feature selection; separate models for Gram-positive and Gram-negative bacteria
models.input_features: Amino acid composition (AAC), dipeptide composition (DPC), pseudo amino acid composition (PseAAC), composition-transition-distribution (CTD), global physicochemical descriptors
models.candidate_reason: Publicly available code and dataset; specific models for Gram+ and Gram-; uses experimentally validated non-AMPs as negatives; suitable for benchmarking.

metrics.description: Deep-AmPEP30: 77%; CalcAMP: ~81%; DRAMP ML model: 92.59% training, 100% test; toxicity model: not directly reported accuracy but recall/F1.
Deep-AmPEP30: 85%; toxicity model: 0.8835 before feature selection; CalcAMP: not explicitly reported.

important_evidence: Deep-AmPEP30 achieved 77% accuracy, AUC-ROC 85%, and was validated by genome screening of Candida glabrata, identifying a potent peptide P3 comparable to ampicillin.
CalcAMP provides separate models for Gram-positive and Gram-negative bacteria, with code and dataset publicly available; accuracy ~81%.
The unnamed AMP predictor from DRAMP 2.0 reported 92.59% training accuracy and 100% test accuracy but lacks a name, public code, or web server; integration into DRAMP is pending.
AMP toxicity prediction model (hybrid) achieved recall 0.876, F1 0.849, focusing on toxicity rather than AMP activity; code available.
uncertainties: The unnamed AMP predictor from DRAMP 2.0 may have been integrated later; check DRAMP website for any prediction tool.
The AMP toxicity prediction model is not an AMP classifier but could be relevant for benchmark filtering; decide on inclusion policy.
Deep-AmPEP30 web server availability should be confirmed; the paper states it supports genome screening, but no code repository found.
CalcAMP provides separate models for Gram+ and Gram-; we need to decide how to handle them in a unified benchmark.
